::: {.tut-standfirst}
Everything Saíra relies on, in one place: the open-source R packages that make the app work, the public data bundled inside the package, and the method credits.
:::

## R packages used

Saíra is built on open-source R packages, all declared as dependencies in [`DESCRIPTION`](https://github.com/rogerio-onza/saira/blob/main/DESCRIPTION) and called explicitly (`package::function()`). No code from these packages is copied into Saíra; they are used as libraries.

### Interface

| Package | What for | License |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [shiny](https://cran.r-project.org/package=shiny) | Web application framework | MIT |
| [bslib](https://cran.r-project.org/package=bslib) | Bootstrap 5 theme and layout | MIT |
| [htmltools](https://cran.r-project.org/package=htmltools) | HTML generation | GPL (≥ 2) |
| [DT](https://cran.r-project.org/package=DT) | Interactive tables | MIT |
| [leaflet](https://cran.r-project.org/package=leaflet) | Interactive maps | MIT |

::: {.callout-note}
Saíra is distributed under **GPL-3** because it uses GPL-licensed packages (among them `CoordinateCleaner`, `countrycode`, `terra`, `florabr` and `faunabr`). The GPL requires that a work depending on these packages keep a compatible license. It is a compatibility choice, not an imposed restriction.
:::

## Data bundled in the package

Some reference data ships inside the package (under `inst/extdata/`) so Saíra can work without a connection on every use. All of it comes from public sources, and the scripts that generate it live in [`data-raw/`](https://github.com/rogerio-onza/saira/tree/main/data-raw).

| Data | Source | License / condition |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Land and country layer (Natural Earth) | [Natural Earth](https://www.naturalearthdata.com/) | Public domain |
| Darwin Core terms | [TDWG · Darwin Core](https://dwc.tdwg.org/) ([repository](https://github.com/tdwg/dwc)) | CC-BY 4.0 |
| Brazilian Official List of Threatened Species | [Portaria MMA nº 148/2022](https://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/portaria-mma-n-148-de-7-de-junho-de-2022-406272733) (flora), [nº 1.704/2026](https://www.in.gov.br/en/web/dou/-/portaria-mma-n-1.704-de-16-de-junho-de-2026-712968917) (terrestrial fauna), [GM/MMA nº 1.667/2026](https://www.in.gov.br/web/dou/-/portaria-gm/mma-n-1.667-de-27-de-abril-de-2026-702075623) (aquatic fauna) | Public government record |
| DwC term synonyms and aliases, country aliases, interface text (i18n) | Authored by Saíra | GPL-3 |

The Darwin Core term list is published by TDWG under **CC-BY 4.0**, which requires attribution, fulfilled by this page and the links above.

## Methods and credits

Beyond its dependencies, Saíra builds on ideas and methodologies published by other projects. These are **not dependencies**: they are method acknowledgements.

- **bdc (Biodiversity Data Cleaning).** Ribeiro, B. R. et al. (2022). *bdc: A toolkit for standardizing, integrating and improving the quality of biodiversity data.* *Methods in Ecology and Evolution.* <https://doi.org/10.1111/2041-210X.13868>. Two of Saíra's coordinate corrections (transposed-coordinate detection and filling country from coordinates) are **independent reimplementations inspired by `bdc`'s approach, with no code reuse**, running on Saíra's own bundled Natural Earth layer. Saíra **does not depend** on the `bdc` package.
- **Sensitive-species generalization (GBIF).** The decision cascade and generalization levels follow GBIF best practices:
  - Chapman, A. D. (2020). *Current Best Practices for Generalizing Sensitive Species Occurrence Data.* GBIF Secretariat. <https://doi.org/10.15468/doc-5jp4-5g10>
  - Chapman, A. D., & Wieczorek, J. R. (2020). *Georeferencing Best Practices.* GBIF Secretariat. <https://doi.org/10.15468/doc-gg7h-s853>
  - Zermoglio, P. F., Chapman, A. D., Wieczorek, J. R., Luna, M. C., & Bloom, D. A. (2020). *Georeferencing Quick Reference Guide.* GBIF Secretariat. <https://doi.org/10.35035/e09p-h128>
